stories.title: Akamai predicts revenue to exceed $7bn in 2028, driven by cloud infrastructure services growth
stories.summary: Edge and cloud firm Akamai is anticipating significant revenue growth over the next two years.
stories.title_zh: Akamai predicts revenue to exceed $7bn in 2028, driven by cloud infrastructure services growth
stories.content:
Edge and cloud firm Akamai is anticipating significant revenue growth over the next two years.

During its earnings call last week, CEO Tom Leighton said that the company is anticipating that total revenue could surpass $7 billion in 2028. "As cloud infrastructure services become a larger portion of our revenue, we expect it to have a strong positive impact on our margins and EPS growth," he added.

Total revenue for the latest quarter was $1.122bn, up 6 percent Year-on-Year (YoY), while cloud infrastructure revenue was $109m, up 34 percent YoY and by far the fastest-growing segment.

Akamai is anticipating that in 2027, the segment could generate $1.1bn to $1.3bn, with a total company revenue growth of 17 to 22 percent.

Driving this is the company's recently signed $11.6bn contract with Anthropic, for which CFO Ed McGowan said that the company has secured approximately 70 percent of the necessary hardware, memory, and other components needed to deliver on this contract.

According to CEO Leighton, the Anthropic contract brought its total of multiyear commitments for CIS signed this year to more than $14 billion, including the May deal also signed with Anthropic, two large deals with unnamed AI companies, and “numerous multimillion-dollar deals with major enterprises around the world.”

Of the large deals, two of the three are already generating revenue and the third is anticipated to commence in Q4 2026. The company is expecting to generate approximately $22m in revenue per megawatt of contracted power, with McGowan stating this is the “floor” as far as pricing goes and applies to the large long-term contracts which typically offer favorable terms to the customers.

Leighton noted that the company has faced some “modest supply chain and third-party data center delays” with two of its contracts and thus is expecting revenue in Q4 to be less than expected, but “won’t impact our outlook for 2027.”

With this in mind, capex for Q3 2026 was lower than expected at $464m, and is expected to jump in Q4 to between $2.445bn and $2.645bn. This includes $1.7bn that is being spent on the Anthropic contract.

Among the strengths listed by Leighton were Akamai’s large existing backbone, which he said has enabled the company to deploy compute capacity at a number of smaller locations more quickly than others who may have to concentrate their compute at fewer large deployments.

Additionally, Akamai is focusing on inference workloads and training for enterprise-sized models, which are primarily CPU-powered. CPUs are less expensive and use less power to run, benefiting Akamai. The company said that its CPU capacity is currently leased out for seven years under the aforementioned contracts.

The company posted a non-GAAP operating margin of 25 percent, down six percentage points YoY, but the company said it expects this to rise above 30 once its large contracts are fully ramped up. Commenting on this, McGowan said: “When you do these big build-outs, you're going to have -- your colocation cost is going to come in ahead of revenue. And the other issue is when you're doing a long-term colo commitment, they do come with price escalators. So you do have to put the straight-line effect of that. So what ends up happening is you end up taking a noncash charge because you're actually booking a cost higher than what you're paying for with colocation.”

Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $435m, down 5 percent.

Following the earnings call, Akamai has announced plans to offer $1.1bn in convertible senior notes due in 2028 and $1.1bn in convertible senior notes due in 2031. Akamai will grant the initial purchasers of the offering an option to purchase up to an additional $150 million in aggregate principal amount of the 2028 Notes and an additional $150 million in aggregate principal amount of the 2031 Notes.
